exam_set.title: Practice Set 3
exam_set.description: Textbook Practice — Book 1, Chapter 3, Practice Set 3

questions.jp: 顧客番号をキーとして顧客データを検索する場合、2分探索を使用するのが適しているものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Kokyaku bangō o kī to shite kokyaku dēta o kensaku suru baai, nibun tansaku o shiyō suru no ga tekishite iru mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: When searching customer data by customer number, which data arrangement suits binary search?

options.label: ア
options.jp: 顧客番号から求めたハッシュ値が指し示す位置に配置されているデータ構造
options.romaji: Kokyaku bangō kara motometa hasshu chi ga sashishimesu ichi ni haichi sarete iru dēta kōzō
options.en: Data placed at positions indicated by a hash value.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 顧客番号に関係なく、ランダムに配置されているデータ構造
options.romaji: Kokyaku bangō ni kankeinaku, randamu ni haichi sarete iru dēta kōzō
options.en: Data arranged randomly regardless of customer number.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 顧客番号の昇順に配置されているデータ構造
options.romaji: Kokyaku bangō no shōjun ni haichi sarete iru dēta kōzō
options.en: Data arranged in ascending customer-number order.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 顧客番号をセルに格納し、セルのアドレス順に配置されているデータ構造
options.romaji: Kokyaku bangō o seru ni kakunō shi, seru no adoresu jun ni haichi sarete iru dēta kōzō
options.en: Customer numbers stored in cells arranged by cell address.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Binary search is like finding a word in a dictionary. You look near the middle, decide whether the target comes before or after it, and discard half the pages. This works only because the dictionary is ordered by the same thing you are searching for.

Technical breakdown:
The search key is 顧客番号, the customer number. Binary search compares the target with a middle customer number. If the target is smaller, it searches only the lower-numbered half; if larger, only the higher-numbered half. That decision is valid only when records are sorted by customer number. Ascending customer-number order provides exactly that condition.

Japanese keywords to remember:
2分探索 = nibun tansaku = binary search
検索キー = kensaku kī = search key
顧客番号 = kokyaku bangō = customer number
昇順 = shōjun = ascending order

Why the best solution works:
When customer numbers are in ascending order, each comparison can safely discard half the remaining records. This gives binary search its efficient O(log n) behavior.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Placement by a hash derived from the customer number describes a hash table and is suitable for hash search, not binary search.

イ:
Random arrangement provides no ordering. A middle comparison cannot tell which half contains the target.

エ:
Cell-address order describes physical or storage order. It helps only if that order also matches the customer-number key, which the option does not state.

Memory trick:
Binary search needs two matches: sorted data and sorting by the search key.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: クイックソートの処理方法を説明したものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Kuitto sōto no shori hōhō o setsumei shita mono wa dore ka.

options.label: ア
options.jp: 既に整列済みのデータ列の正しい位置に、データを追加する操作を繰り返していく方法である。
options.romaji: Sude ni seiretsu-zumi no dēta retsu no tadashii ichi ni, dēta o tsuika suru sōsa o kurikaeshite iku hōhō de aru.
options.en: Repeatedly insert data into its correct position in a sorted sequence.

options.label: イ
options.jp: データ中の最小値を求め、次にそれを除いた部分の中から最小値を求める。この操作を繰り返していく方法である。
options.romaji: Dēta chū no saishōchi o motome, tsugi ni sore o nojuita bubun no naka kara saishōchi o motomeru. Kono sōsa o kurikaeshite iku hōhō de aru.
options.en: Repeatedly select the smallest remaining value.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 適当な基準値を選び、それよりも小さな値のグループと大きな値のグループにデータを分割する。同様にして、グループの中で基準値を選び、それぞれのグループを分割する。この操作を繰り返していく方法である。
options.romaji: Tekitō na kijunchi o erabi, sore yori mo chiisana atai no gurūpu to ōkina atai no gurūpu ni dēta o bunkatsu suru. Dōyō ni kurikaesu hōhō de aru.
options.en: Choose a pivot, split data into smaller and larger groups, and repeat.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 隣り合ったデータの比較と入替えを繰り返すことによって、小さな値のデータを次第に端の方に移していく方法である。
options.romaji: Tonariawatta dēta no hikaku to irekae o kurikaesu koto ni yotte, chiisana atai no dēta o shidai ni hashi no hō ni utsushite iku hōhō de aru.
options.en: Repeatedly compare and swap adjacent data, moving small values toward an end.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Quicksort chooses one value as a divider, called a pivot. Values smaller than the pivot go into one group and larger values into another. It then performs the same job inside each smaller group until everything is ordered.

Technical breakdown:
Step 1: choose a pivot.
Step 2: partition the data into values smaller than the pivot and values larger than the pivot.
Step 3: recursively repeat the pivot-and-partition process for each group.
When every group has zero or one item, the whole sequence is sorted. The wording “choose a reference value” and “divide into smaller and larger groups” is quicksort's signature.

Japanese keywords to remember:
クイックソート = kuikku sōto = quicksort
基準値 = kijunchi = pivot
分割 = bunkatsu = partition
繰り返す = kurikaesu = repeat

Why the best solution works:
ウ describes both essential parts of quicksort: partitioning around a pivot and recursively repeating on the resulting groups.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
Adding each item into its correct position in an already sorted portion describes insertion sort.

イ:
Repeatedly finding and removing the smallest remaining value describes selection sort.

エ:
Repeatedly comparing and swapping adjacent elements describes bubble sort.

Memory trick:
Insertion inserts, selection selects the minimum, bubble swaps neighbors, quicksort pivots and partitions.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: 10進法で5桁の数a1a2a3a4a5を、ハッシュ法を用いて配列に格納したい。ハッシュ関数をmod(a1＋a2＋a3＋a4＋a5, 13)とし、求めたハッシュ値に対応する位置の配列要素に格納する場合、54321は配列のどの位置に入るか。ここで、mod(x, 13)は、xを13で割った余りとする。
questions.romaji: Jūshinhō de go-keta no sū a1a2a3a4a5 o, hasshu hō o mochiite hairē ni kakunō shitai. 54321 wa hairē no dono ichi ni hairu ka.
questions.en: Using hash mod(a1+a2+a3+a4+a5,13), at which array position is 54321 stored?

options.label: ア
options.romaji: ichi

options.label: イ
options.romaji: ni

options.label: ウ
options.romaji: nana

options.label: エ
options.romaji: jū-ichi

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
The hash function turns the five-digit number into a small array position. First add the digits. Then divide by 13 and use the remainder as the position.

Technical breakdown:
For 54321, the digits are 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1.
5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 15.
The function is mod(sum, 13). “mod” means the remainder after division.
15 = 13 × 1 + 2, so 15 mod 13 = 2.
Therefore 54321 is stored at array position 2.

Japanese keywords to remember:
ハッシュ法 = hasshu-hō = hashing
ハッシュ関数 = hasshu kansū = hash function
余り = amari = remainder
配列要素 = hairē yōso = array element

Why the best solution works:
Applying the stated function exactly produces remainder 2, so the corresponding array element is position 2.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
1 is the quotient when 15 is divided by 13, but mod returns the remainder, not the quotient.

ウ:
7 is not obtained from either the digit sum or its remainder modulo 13.

エ:
11 is also not the remainder of 15 divided by 13; it may result from an unrelated calculation.

Memory trick:
For mod questions, write dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder. The last number is the hash value.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: 探索方法とその実行時間のオーダーの適切な組合せはどれか。ここで、探索するデータの数をnとし、ハッシュ値が衝突する確率は無視できるほど小さいものとする。
questions.romaji: Tansaku hōhō to sono jikkō jikan no ōdā no tekisetsu na kumiawase wa dore ka.
questions.en: Which combination of search method and execution-time order is appropriate? Hash collisions are negligible.

options.label: ア
options.jp: 2分探索：log2n、線形探索：n、ハッシュ探索：1
options.romaji: Nibun tansaku: log2 n, senkei tansaku: n, hasshu tansaku: ichi
options.en: Binary: log2 n; linear: n; hash: 1.

options.label: イ
options.jp: 2分探索：nlog2n、線形探索：n、ハッシュ探索：log2n
options.romaji: Nibun tansaku: n log2 n; senkei tansaku: n; hasshu tansaku: log2 n
options.en: Binary: n log2 n; linear: n; hash: log2 n.

options.label: ウ
options.jp: 2分探索：nlog2n、線形探索：n²、ハッシュ探索：1
options.romaji: Nibun tansaku: n log2 n; senkei tansaku: n nijō; hasshu tansaku: ichi
options.en: Binary: n log2 n; linear: n squared; hash: 1.

options.label: エ
options.jp: 2分探索：n²、線形探索：1、ハッシュ探索：n
options.romaji: Nibun tansaku: n nijō; senkei tansaku: ichi; hasshu tansaku: n
options.en: Binary: n squared; linear: 1; hash: n.

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
The three searches move through data differently. Binary search repeatedly cuts the remaining area in half. Linear search walks through items one by one. A good hash search calculates where to jump directly.

Technical breakdown:
Binary search halves the candidate set each step, so its time is O(log₂ n).
Linear search may inspect all n records, so its time is O(n).
Under the question's assumption that hash collisions are negligibly rare, hash search computes a location and accesses it directly, giving expected O(1).
Thus the correct row is log₂ n, n, 1.

Japanese keywords to remember:
実行時間のオーダー = jikkō jikan no ōdā = order of execution time
線形探索 = senkei tansaku = linear search
ハッシュ探索 = hasshu tansaku = hash search
衝突 = shōtotsu = collision

Why the best solution works:
ア pairs each method with its characteristic growth: halving gives logarithmic time, walking gives linear time, and direct hash access gives expected constant time under the stated collision assumption.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ:
It assigns O(n log n) to binary search and O(log n) to hash search. O(n log n) is common for efficient comparison sorting, while good hashing is expected O(1).

ウ:
It again gives binary search O(n log n) and makes linear search O(n²). A single linear scan is O(n), not quadratic.

エ:
It says binary search is O(n²), linear search O(1), and hash search O(n), reversing the normal advantages. None of these matches the methods.

Memory trick:
Binary halves = log; linear walks = n; hash jumps = 1.

Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: nの階乗を再帰的に計算する関数F(n)の定義において、aに入れるべき式はどれか。ここで、nは非負の整数とする。n＞0のとき、F(n)＝a。n＝0のとき、F(n)＝1。
questions.romaji: n no kaijō o saikiteki ni keisan suru kansū F(n) no teigi ni oite, a ni ireru beki shiki wa dore ka.
questions.en: In recursive factorial function F(n), which expression belongs in a? F(0)=1.

options.label: ア
options.romaji: n purasu F(n mainasu ichi)

options.label: イ
options.romaji: n mainasu ichi purasu F(n)

options.label: ウ
options.romaji: n kakeru F(n mainasu ichi)

options.label: エ
options.romaji: n mainasu ichi kakeru F(n)

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A recursive factorial function solves n! by asking for the factorial of the next smaller number. It must eventually reach a simple stopping case. Here the stopping case is F(0) = 1.

Technical breakdown:
For n > 0, factorial follows F(n) = n × F(n−1).
Example:
F(3) = 3 × F(2)
= 3 × 2 × F(1)
= 3 × 2 × 1 × F(0)
= 3 × 2 × 1 × 1
= 6.
Each recursive call reduces n by 1, so it reaches the base case F(0) = 1.

Japanese keywords to remember:
階乗 = kaijō = factorial
再帰的 = saikiteki = recursively
基底条件 = kitei jōken = base case
非負の整数 = hifu no seisū = nonnegative integer

Why the best solution works:
ウ multiplies n by the factorial of n−1. It both matches the mathematical definition of factorial and makes progress toward the base case.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア:
n + F(n−1) adds rather than multiplies, so it calculates a sum instead of a factorial.

イ:
n−1 + F(n) still refers to F(n) itself and does not reduce the recursive argument. It also uses addition.

エ:
(n−1) × F(n) also calls F(n) again with the same argument, so it does not approach F(0) and would recurse indefinitely.

Memory trick:
A valid recursion needs an operation, a smaller argument, and a base case: n × F(n−1), then F(0) = 1.

Correct answer: ウ
